manifest.title: Butaca
manifest.appDescription: Unofficial native Jellyfin client - not affiliated with Jellyfin

packages.shortDescription: A native Jellyfin client for LG webOS, drawn by the TV, not a browser
packages.description:
An unofficial, native Jellyfin client for LG webOS televisions.

The official Jellyfin clients on these sets are web apps, and on older hardware it shows:
shelves stutter, posters open a beat late. Butaca draws its interface directly on the GPU and
hands video to the television's own hardware decoder, the same silicon the built-in apps use.

**What it does**

* Point it at your Jellyfin server, sign in with the account you already use, or approve a Quick
  Connect code from a device that is already signed in
* Sign in to more than one server and switch between them in Settings, each with its own token
* Browse libraries with a grid, sort, filter (unwatched only among them), an A to Z rail and a
  Favorites tab, and search across everything the active server offers
* Direct play of H.264 and HEVC, including 4K, 10 bit and Dolby Vision as the server reports it;
  the server transcodes when the set cannot decode the file, and Auto follows a link whose speed
  changes
* Resume, seek and scrub, chapters from the server, audio and subtitle track switching, Skip Intro
  and Skip Credits where the server has the markers, Up Next, and progress reported back to your
  server
* ASS and SSA subtitles rendered by the set with their styles, positioning and embedded fonts;
  image subtitles (PGS, VobSub) unpacked during direct play; subtitle size and position adjustable
* A developer id and a release id are separate apps, so a nightly or a debug build never touches
  the install you watch with

**Scope - please read before installing**

* **Films and television only.** No music, no photos, no live television and no DVR.
* **One server at a time.** Several can be configured, and the screens show the active one.
* **The address you type is the address it talks to.** A server reached by name needs `https://`.
  A plain `http://` address is accepted only for an IP literal the app can prove is on your own
  local network, because it will not send a password over plain HTTP to anything else.
* **It talks to your server and to nothing else.** There is no account with the author, no
  telemetry, no analytics and no crash reporting compiled in. The password you type is used once;
  what stays on the television is an access token your server can revoke.
* **Not every 2019 set plays video installed through Developer Mode**, and it is not this app's
  bug to fix: some k5lp and k3lp sets have a Developer Mode sandbox that withholds a device the
  video path needs. The app detects it and says so. On a rooted set with Homebrew Channel the
  failure screen offers Repair; without root there is no fix. Some 2018 sets on firmware reporting
  platform release 3.9.3 can sign in and browse but have not been seen to start video, and there
  is a crash reported on sets built on LG's k6hp chip that has not been reproduced.

**Compatibility**

This needs **webOS 4.0 or newer**; older firmware does not start it. The maintainer develops and
watches on a 2019 LG set, and the release audit records which televisions each version was
actually verified on, which third-party reports exist and what they said. A report that it works
on your set is as useful as one that it fails.

**Root is not needed.** A regular set in Developer Mode runs everything except the Repair above.
Developer Mode expires and has to be renewed, and when it does LG removes the apps installed
through it. A rooted set with Homebrew Channel has no expiry.

Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Jellyfin or LG Electronics.

Source, screenshots and issues: https://github.com/gnacho/butaca

packages.description:
# HotsOff

> Patch-based ad-block layer for the stock Hotstar app on rooted LG webOS TVs.
> A sister project of [AmazOff](https://github.com/azoffshowy/AmazOff).

**HotsOff** patches the installed Hotstar app:
- Remove live / match ads (requests the clean, non ad-stitched stream)
- Remove pre-rolls, mid-rolls and the ads shown under the player when paused
- Remove the "Upgrade" / "Subscribe" button and subscription nudges
- Suppress third-party telemetry (Coralogix, Google Tag Manager, Moat, Firebase logging)

Because the stock app itself is patched, every launch path opens the ad-free version.
HotsOff does not touch DRM, subscriptions or premium content.

## Status

- **Development stage:** early / experimental
- **Tested on:** LG C2, webOS 25 (rooted)

## How it works

The Hotstar webOS app is a thin launcher for `livingroom.hotstar.com`. HotsOff places a
WebAppManager user script (`webOSUserScripts/userScript.js`) in the installed Hotstar app
folder, which removes ad data from the app's network traffic. **Stop Service** removes it again.

## Usage

1. Launch **HotsOff**
2. Press **Start Service**
3. **Recommended:** enable **Autostart** so the patch is re-applied after Hotstar updates

manifest.appDescription: Preserves Developer Mode, its official session token, and session time without root.

packages.shortDescription: Keeps Developer Mode on by resetting its power-off counter, no root required.
packages.description:
Keeps Developer Mode enabled on LG webOS TVs without root.


webOS turns Developer Mode off after 11 real power-offs, and the next
boot removes every dev-installed app. The official startup script clears
that counter only when the network is ready at boot, so it can still
build up while the session is valid. Dev Mode Forever runs a small
service at every boot that:

- Resets the power-off counter once it reaches 8, by switching Developer
  Mode off and back on through the system devmode service
- Renews the official Developer Mode session, then backs up and validates
  the session token before every reset, and aborts if any step fails
- Renews the session at startup when fewer than 7 days remain
- Shows Developer Mode, token, session time and counter status, with
  Check now, Extend session and Force toggle actions


A counter reset **reboots the TV**. Expect one controlled reboot per
about 8 real power-offs, at most once every 24 hours. Standby with Quick
Start+ and reboots do not count as power-offs.


Developer Mode must be enabled through LG's official Developer Mode app,
and that app must stay installed. A network connection and a valid
official session token are needed to renew the session. No account
password is stored or sent. Rooted TVs do not need this app: Homebrew
Channel's startup script already clears the counter.


No root required. Free and open source under the Apache-2.0 license.
Source code: https://github.com/lennylxx/lg-devmode-forever

* **Top carousel** instead of LG ads: continue watching, next up, recently
  added, favorites or a random pick. Each item gets artwork composed on the TV:
  the poster, the backdrop and the title logo (or the title in large type).
* **Trailers**: the item's local Jellyfin trailer, or the YouTube link from its
  metadata. They are downloaded in advance on the TV (480p, falling back to 720p
  then 1080p) and played in the carousel over the poster. The home screen turns
  the sound on when the carousel is focused.
* **Banner and rows**: the banner next to recent inputs, and rows for continue
  watching (with a progress bar), next up and recently added.

* Selecting an item launches the Jellyfin app on its details page.
* Sign-in with **Quick Connect**: no password to type with the remote.
* Interface in English, French, German, Spanish and Italian.

## Requirements

* A rooted LG TV with the Homebrew Channel.
* webOS 10 or later (the Flutter home screen). Tested on webOS 10.3.
* A Jellyfin server on the same network, with Quick Connect enabled.
* The official Jellyfin app on the TV, to play what you select.

## Setup

1. Install JellyHome and open it once: it installs its boot hook and enables
   the home screen patch.
2. Search for your server, then sign in with Quick Connect from your phone.
3. Choose what goes where, then press *Apply to home screen*.

## How it works

The home screen app is not modified. A small library, loaded into it at launch,
rewrites the replies it gets from system services, following rules generated
by a background service on the TV. The patch lives in bind mounts that are gone
after a reboot, and a guard disables it if the home screen crashes three times
in a minute.

Your Jellyfin session stays on the TV, readable by root only. Trailers and
artwork are cached on the TV's internal storage and cleaned up automatically.

To remove it, use *Disable patch* in the app, then uninstall it from the
Homebrew Channel.

Source code and details: https://github.com/Smeagolworms4/lg-jellyfin-homeapp

Claude (Anthropic) was used as an assistant for the implementation and
documentation. The maintainer is an experienced developer who led the
development, reviewed the generated code, and tested the app and its features

packages.description:
An unofficial, native Jellyfin client for LG webOS televisions.

Native Jelly draws its interface directly on the GPU and hands video to the television's own hardware decoder, the same one the built-in apps use. It is built from [PlxNative](https://github.com/GLinnik21/plx-native)'s native player and interface, rebuilt to sign in to and play from your own Jellyfin server.

**What it does**

* Sign in with your Jellyfin server's address, then a user name and password or a Quick Connect code approved from another device
* Up to twelve Jellyfin users on one television, with **Who's watching?** at start
* Your libraries, Home, Search and Continue Watching
* Plays a file directly when the television can decode it; anything else is remuxed or transcoded by your server, which also records where you stopped and what you finished
* Choose audio and subtitle tracks, including image subtitles, and adjust subtitle timing, size and position
* English, Spanish and Belarusian, following the television's language

**Scope — please read before installing**

* **Video playback is verified on one television:** an LG C1 (2021) on webOS 6.5.3, including transcoded films with subtitles, seeking and track changes. On every other firmware from webOS 4.0 up the app is only known to start. If you try it on another set, please [report what happened](https://github.com/sostk/native-jelly/issues), whether it worked or not.
* **Movies and TV shows only.** No music, photos or live TV.
* **A server reached over plain http receives your password unencrypted.** Native Jelly asks before it connects to one, with a stronger warning for an internet address, and **Settings → Unencrypted connections** lists and revokes what you allowed. Use your server's https address when it has one.
* **Known issues:** playback can fail from a server reached over https through a reverse proxy; a re-encode is always H.264; Auto quality away from home has not been tried on a television.

Crash reports and usage analytics are both off until you choose to share them; the [privacy policy](https://github.com/sostk/native-jelly/blob/main/PRIVACY.md) lists exactly what each contains.

Screenshots show openly licensed films from the Blender Foundation and others, credited in [CREDITS.md](https://github.com/sostk/native-jelly/blob/main/docs/screenshots/CREDITS.md).

Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by the Jellyfin project or LG Electronics.

packages.shortDescription: Music Assistant TV companion: MilkDrop visuals, artwork, lyrics and playback
packages.description:
# Afterglow

An unofficial [Music Assistant](https://music-assistant.io/) player for your TV. It shows
the album artwork, word-by-word lyrics and the queue, lets you browse, search and play
from the remote, and draws MilkDrop visuals in time with whatever your speakers are
playing, from the waveform Music Assistant's **MilkDrop Visualizer** plugin streams a
few seconds ahead.

![Lyrics view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaydenGriffin/afterglow/main/docs/screenshots/lyrics.jpg)

## What it does

- **Album, Lyrics and Visuals views.** Complete artwork; timed lyrics with word-by-word karaoke where the lyrics have word timing; MilkDrop on its own, with a track card, or behind the artwork and lyrics.
- **Browse and Search** your Music Assistant library: recently played, favourites, radio, playlists and albums. Play now, play next, add to the queue or start radio.
- **Queue**: play, move and remove songs, shuffle, repeat, crossfade, volume and sleep timer. **Play on** moves the music to another speaker; **Speakers together** joins or leaves a sync group.
- **Idle poster**: when nothing plays, the paused song or recent music, one OK away.
- **Play on this TV**: the TV itself becomes a Music Assistant speaker through Sendspin.
- 395 MilkDrop presets; **Scan presets** measures each one on *your* TV and keeps the ones it runs smoothly. Favourites are shared with Music Assistant's own MilkDrop favourites.
- Remote media keys: play/pause, stop, fast-forward and rewind.
- Kind to OLEDs: the screensaver is held off only while music plays, and the picture drifts against burn-in.

![Album view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaydenGriffin/afterglow/main/docs/screenshots/album.jpg)

## Requirements

- Music Assistant 2.10 or newer, on the same network, with the MilkDrop Visualizer plugin added (Settings → Plugins) for the visuals.
- Speakers Music Assistant streams to itself (Sonos, Chromecast, AirPlay, Squeezelite, …). A speaker playing something on its own, such as Spotify straight from the Spotify app, carries nothing it can draw.
- A TV with WebGL2 (LG's 2020 models onward). Tested on an LG OLED C1 (webOS 6). No root required.

## Setting up

On first launch, sign in with Music Assistant's address and your username and password.
The TV gets its own long-lived token, named after it, which you can revoke in Music
Assistant's settings or with **Log out**; the password is not stored.
Then run **Scan presets** once. The [setup guide](https://github.com/HaydenGriffin/afterglow/blob/main/docs/install.md)
walks through everything, and [Settings and remote keys](https://github.com/HaydenGriffin/afterglow/blob/main/docs/settings.md) lists every option.

## Privacy

Afterglow talks to your Music Assistant server. The one exception is lyrics: when Music
Assistant has none for a song, the TV asks [lrclib.net](https://lrclib.net) directly,
sending the song's title and artist. **Display → Lyrics → Online lyrics → Off** stops that.

![Sign in](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaydenGriffin/afterglow/main/docs/screenshots/sign-in.jpg)

## Source

[github.com/HaydenGriffin/afterglow](https://github.com/HaydenGriffin/afterglow) (MIT), based on Michael Nestrud's
[viz-man](https://github.com/mnestrud/viz-man). Rendering by the
[Music Assistant fork](https://github.com/music-assistant/butterchurn) of
[Butterchurn](https://github.com/jberg/butterchurn) and the butterchurn-presets packs (MIT);
Sendspin playback by [sendspin-js](https://github.com/Sendspin/sendspin-js) (Apache-2.0).

packages.title: DTS Enabler

manifest.title: DTS Enabler
manifest.appDescription: Restore DTS and Dolby TrueHD/MLP audio on rooted LG webOS 25 TVs, including DTS and TrueHD in MKV, MP4, TS and M2TS. Also offers exact-firmware experimental DTS support for C2/G2 via explicit opt-in. Requires the Homebrew Channel + root.

packages.shortDescription: Restore DTS and Dolby TrueHD/MLP audio on rooted LG webOS 25 TVs, including DTS and TrueHD in MKV, MP4, TS and M2TS. Also offers exact-firmware experimental DTS support for C2/G2 via explicit opt-in. Requires the Homebrew Channel + root.
packages.description:
## DTS Enabler — DTS + Dolby TrueHD/MLP audio for rooted LG TVs

LG removed DTS decoding from some TV generations and kept it in others. This app
works out which one you have and, where the decoder is missing, restores **DTS** and
**Dolby TrueHD / MLP** playback. Audio is decoded to native **discrete multichannel**
PCM — there is no stereo downmix in the pipeline.

It also tells you when you do **not** need it, rather than reporting a working TV as
unsupported.

### What you get, by generation
- **C5 / G5 and later (webOS 25)** — LG ships no DTS or TrueHD decoder. This is the
  **verified** target: DTS and DTS-HD (core) in **MKV, MP4, TS and M2TS**, and Dolby
  **TrueHD / MLP** in **MKV, TS and M2TS**. Includes loudness controls (make-up gain,
  a DRC preset and a dialogue boost), a self-test and a play-by-ear check.
- **C4 / G4 / M4 / T4 (2024)** — DTS is **native and working**. Reported as needing
  nothing; no mechanism is offered.
- **C3 / G3 / M3 (2023)** — LG restored DTS here, but on some builds the decoder is
  present and switched off. Reported as such, with no mechanism shipped for that
  generation yet.
- **C2 / G2 (2022)** — an **experimental** profile for one exact analyzed firmware,
  behind a two-step opt-in. Firmware-matched only; **never** reported as hardware
  verified, because no rooted C2/G2 was available to test on.
- **B2 / B3** — recognised and explicitly refused, with family-specific reasons.
- **CX-class (webOS 3–6)** — the inherited mechanism, carried over and unverified by
  this fork. The original `lgstreamer/dts_restore` is the better tool there.

### Safety
- **Reversible, with one stated exception** — the codec/demuxer/config overrides are
  bind-mounts over the stock files, so Disable/Uninstall (or a reboot) revert them. The
  one persistent write is the GStreamer plugin registry, a `cp -f`; Disable/Uninstall
  revert it by regenerating a clean stock registry from the pristine on-disk plugins. If
  a bind is busy because a live process has it mapped, the fallback is a lazy detach and
  a reboot clears it.
- **Applies its mechanism only to TVs it should** — before binding anything, the
  installer and boot hook fingerprint the stock plugins they would shadow and check them
  against a table of verified sets, **and** check the model. Stock plugins can be
  byte-identical across models, so a hash match on a model nobody has tested is reported
  as exactly that and requires the explicit two-step "Try anyway (experimental)" opt-in,
  which itself requires the payload's dynamic dependencies to resolve on that TV.
  Anything unrecognised is refused with the probed values shown for reporting.
- **Fail-safe boot hook** — re-applies automatically on reboot, and stands itself down
  if a firmware update changes the GStreamer version or the stock plugins it was verified
  against, so normal playback is never affected. It also self-heals: if the app is removed
  while still enabled, the next boot drops the binds, regenerates the stock registry and
  unlinks the hook.

### Requirements
- A **rooted** LG TV with the Homebrew Channel (uses its root exec service)
- webOS 7.4 or newer

### Notes
- Decode-to-PCM only; DTS/TrueHD **bitstream passthrough** is out of scope, and DTS:X /
  TrueHD-Atmos **object audio** cannot be delivered — LG's only Atmos-capable decoder
  accepts neither DTS nor TrueHD input.
- DTS-HD MA decodes its lossy core (no XLL lossless extension). TrueHD decodes its full
  base channel bed; Atmos objects are dropped.
- Loudness controls are webOS 25 only, by design: they exist inside decoders this project
  builds, and on generations where LG's own decoder still works it handles loudness itself.
- While enabled, gst-libav's software decoders come from our ffmpeg 4.4 build rather than
  LG's ffmpeg 5 build, because the TrueHD-capable `libgstlibav.so` replaces LG's.
- Open source, mixed licenses: the app, the demuxers and the libav/ffmpeg payload are
  LGPL-2.1-or-later; the DTS decoder links libdca and is GPL-2.0-or-later. Build scripts
  and patched sources are in the project repo, which is the corresponding-source offer.

Source and documentation: https://github.com/josippapez/dts_restore_plus

manifest.title: GStreamer DV MKV Patcher
manifest.appDescription: Play MKV files in Dolby Vision instead of HDR10 on a rooted LG TV, by patching the webOS GStreamer matroska demuxer (webOS 22 verified; webOS 6/C1 and webOS 5 experimental)

packages.shortDescription: Dolby Vision from MKV files on webOS 22 instead of HDR10 (root)
packages.description:
> MKV files play in real Dolby Vision instead of HDR10, by patching the webOS system player's GStreamer matroska demuxer.

LG's webOS plays Dolby Vision from MP4 and TS, but on webOS 22 the MKV demuxer of its system player
(GStreamer plugin `libgstmatroska.so`) ignores the Dolby Vision configuration in MKV files, so every
app falls back to HDR10. LG fixed this only in webOS 25.

This app puts an improved demuxer over LG's original at startup - built from **LG's own source** with
LG's Dolby Vision detection from webOS 25. It works in every app that uses LG's media pipeline: Emby,
Plex, the LG media player, USB and DLNA. **Your MKV files are not changed.**

## Features

- Switch on/off, status, logs, compatibility check, remove everything (English/German)
- Optional **profile 7 -> 8.1** conversion for UHD Blu-ray remuxes (enhancement layer dropped,
  RPU rewritten with libdovi like `dovi_tool -m 2`)
- **Autostart is optional** ("Load automatically at boot"): by default the patch lives in RAM and is
  gone after a reboot; autostart re-applies it at each cold boot where the Homebrew Channel boot hook
  exists (firmware-dependent)
- Root check on every start; without root all actions are locked

## Safety

- **RAM only:** a bind mount over the system file. Nothing is written to firmware partitions; switch
  off or reboot and LG's original is back.
- The plugin is chosen by GStreamer version and load-checked in an isolated instance before overlaying;
  unknown or unusual files keep LG's behaviour and the demuxer never posts an error.
- The patch is copied to `/media/developer/mkvdv/`; with autostart enabled it stays active when the app

packages.shortDescription: VPN client for rooted LG webOS TVs (sing-box)
packages.description:
Whole-TV VPN client for rooted LG webOS TVs, built on [sing-box](https://github.com/SagerNet/sing-box).
Bring your own server: no VPN servers are provided.

Features:

- VLESS (TLS, Reality, Vision; TCP, WebSocket, gRPC, HTTPUpgrade), VMess, Trojan, Shadowsocks, Hysteria2 and TUIC
  profiles, as share links, subscriptions or sing-box JSON outbounds; links from Marzban, 3x-ui, Remnawave and
  Hiddify panels are accepted
- New links that turn off certificate checks are refused, so nobody on the network path can impersonate the server
  (such profiles saved by 0.6.1 or older keep working and are labelled "no certificate check")
- Profiles are added from a phone by QR code over the local network, or from a USB stick
- All TV IPv4 traffic goes through the tunnel, with DNS over HTTPS inside it; external IPv6 is blocked while
  connected; the local network stays reachable
- If the server fails, the normal network is restored and the connection is retried; an independent watchdog
  restores the network if the controller hangs
- Optional connection when the TV turns on (off by default)
- The app installs and updates its components (sing-box core and controller) by itself when opened; it installs
  them only from its signed package and checks the core against a pinned SHA-256
- Root work is done by the app's own Luna service with a fixed set of actions; the interface never builds shell
  commands, and Homebrew Channel is used only to give that service root
- English and Russian interface, following the TV language
- "Remove MEDZH VPN completely" in the app stops the VPN, restores DNS and routes, and deletes its components

Requirements:

- Rooted TV with Homebrew Channel showing "Root OK"
- ARM processor, built-in Node.js 14 or newer (webOS 24 and later), `/dev/net/tun`, `ip rule` and `connmanctl`;
  the app checks all of these before it installs its components

Notes:

- Beta: tested on one model so far (LG 55UA75009LA, webOS 25). Compatibility reports are welcome.
- No kill switch: while the VPN is not connected, TV traffic goes over the normal connection.
- While the QR code is shown, the TV serves a one-time import page over plain HTTP on the local network.
- To uninstall, use "Remove MEDZH VPN completely" in the app first. Removing the app only from the TV menu or
  Homebrew Channel leaves its components and profiles in `/media/developer/tv-vpn`; the VPN then stays off after
  the next restart.
- The app id changed in 0.7.0. If 0.6.x is installed, open the new app: it removes the old one and keeps profiles
  and settings.

Source: https://github.com/steam20011972-code/tv-vpn (MIT). The bundled sing-box is GPL-3.0-or-later.

then connect with **TCP, XHTTP or gRPC**. The VPN runs on the TV, while
your phone manages it through the local CVPN Connect panel.

**TCP, XHTTP and gRPC are Xray transport modes, not separate VPN protocols.**
Compatible VLESS/Reality setups are supported; gRPC also supports TLS.

**Features**

- **TCP / XHTTP / gRPC transports** for supported Xray VLESS configurations.
  Use compatible Reality settings, or TLS with gRPC.
- Import `vless://` links, compatible HTTPS subscriptions or supported
  Xray JSON from **any provider**. A CVPN subscription is optional.
- Connect, disconnect, select a server, refresh subscriptions and check status
  from the local **CVPN Connect** browser interface.
- Pair a phone by scanning the QR code shown on the TV and using a temporary PIN.
- Russian and English interface with remote-control-friendly TV dialogs.
- One All-in-One IPK including the launcher, ARMv7 backend, Xray-core and
  recovery scripts. Components are prepared locally on first run, without
  downloading extra executables onto the TV.

**Requirements**

- An LG TV with working **root**, Homebrew Channel's root service and TUN.
- Compatible ARMv7 / 32-bit userspace, including supported 64-bit kernel TVs.
- A trusted home network and a compatible VPN endpoint/configuration.

**Important limitations**

- The VPN handles **IPv4 only**. An active IPv6 default route prevents connection.
- **No universal kill switch** and no VPN auto-connect at TV startup.
- The control panel uses **unencrypted HTTP on LAN port 8765**. Do not expose
  that port to the internet or use the panel on untrusted networks.
- **Owner-tested on four LG TVs:** 55UK6450PLC (webOS 4.4.3-22),

packages.description:
# Launcher

A minimalist home screen: a greeting and clock, a row of your apps, a row of your
inputs (Live TV and HDMI, with the names set in the TV's input settings), and a way
back to LG's own home.

- Choose which apps and inputs appear, and re-order them (hold OK)
- Follows the TV's 12/24-hour clock setting
- Remote-first navigation; the Magic Remote pointer still works
- **No root required.** No background service or startup scripts
- Optional (off by default): on rooted TVs, read the full installed-app list and real
  icons through the Homebrew Channel

It doesn't take over the HOME button. On rooted TVs you can map a button to it with
LG Input Hook (app ID `works.partridge.webos-launcher`).

Tested on an LG OLED C1 (2021) with webOS 6.5 only. See the
[README](https://github.com/partridgeworks/webos-launcher#compatibility-and-testing).
